title: Rock, paper, scissors referee
prompt:
Referee one round of rock, paper, scissors. The input holds two moves, player 1's and then player 2's, each written as a number: `0` for rock, `1` for paper, `2` for scissors. Paper covers rock, scissors cut paper, and rock breaks scissors.

Print exactly one line:

- `player 1 wins` or `player 2 wins`
- `draw` when both players pick the same move
- `invalid move` when either number is outside 0 to 2; then `main` returns 1 instead of 0, so whoever ran the program can tell it failed

The starter reads both moves into `p1_r` and `p2_r` and holds every message you need. Hint: write out player 1's move minus player 2's for all nine rounds. Only five different gaps turn up, and each one always means the same result.

## what is checked

- with the input `1 0` the program prints `player 1 wins` and returns 0
- the decisions are made with `cmp`
- the checker also referees rounds you do not see: every winner, a draw, and moves just outside the range
starter:
// referee one round of rock, paper, scissors
// moves: 0 = rock, 1 = paper, 2 = scissors

define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(p1_r, x19)
define(p2_r, x20)

.data
fmt_in:     .string "%ld %ld"
msg_p1:     .string "player 1 wins\n"
msg_p2:     .string "player 2 wins\n"
msg_draw:   .string "draw\n"
msg_bad:    .string "invalid move\n"

.bss
.balign 8
p1_m:       .skip 8
p2_m:       .skip 8

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read both moves
        ldr     x1, =p1_m
        ldr     x2, =p2_m
        bl      scanf

        ldr     x9, =p1_m
        ldr     p1_r, [x9]
        ldr     x9, =p2_m
        ldr     p2_r, [x9]

        // TODO: if either move is outside 0 to 2, print msg_bad and
        // return 1. Otherwise print exactly one of msg_p1, msg_p2 or
        // msg_draw, and return 0.

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
